messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

**Proposal: one quarter of engineering capacity for debt paydown**

I'm asking that we give Q3 to maintenance instead of features.

The argument is arithmetic, not principle. Our median PR now takes 6.2 days from open to merge; a year ago it took 2.8. CI accounts for most of the gap. The suite runs 47 minutes and fails at random about one run in five, so engineers rerun it, go do something else, and check back after lunch. Separately, roughly 40% of Q2 engineering hours went to unplanned work: incidents, hotfixes, and slow excavation into why the billing service and the account service define "customer" differently.

Three fixes, in order. Break up the monolithic test suite and quarantine the flaky tests. Finish retiring the second ORM we half-migrated to in 2024. Collapse the two customer models into a single service. None of this is novel work. We know how to do all three, and we have postponed all three four times.

The price is real: a quarter of eight engineers is a quarter of roadmap, and two of the customer commitments currently sitting in Q3 move to Q4.

So the trade is one visible slip now against a delivery rate that keeps getting worse. Postpone again and this same memo lands next year with uglier numbers and a longer list.

I'd like an answer by the 15th so we can plan Q3 around one path or the other. I'm glad to walk through the incident data first.

— [name], Eng Lead

Numbers are placeholders. Substitute your real CI timings, incident share, and headcount before sending; the whole argument rests on them.
